checks.question: Are there classes/modules with excessive responsibilities, many unrelated methods, broad dependencies, or frequent unrelated changes (god object/module)? (ARC-001)

onYes.title: Fix god object (ARC-001): split by cohesive responsibility
onYes.prompt:
Problem: God objects concentrate too many responsibilities, becoming hard to change, test, and reason about.

Find all instances: Search for very large classes/modules with many unrelated methods, broad dependency fan-out, or high change frequency for unrelated reasons.

Fix correctly: Split into cohesive units organized by responsibility and reason-to-change; extract collaborators behind clear interfaces.

Constraints: Preserve behavior; refactor incrementally with tests. Don't create speculative abstractions (ARC-016).

Acceptance: Responsibilities are separated cohesively. Ensure existing tests pass and add tests for extracted units.

checks.question: Are there functions that mostly inspect or manipulate another object's data instead of their own module's state (feature envy)? (ARC-002)

onYes.title: Fix feature envy (ARC-002): move behavior to the data it uses
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Functions that operate mainly on another object's data indicate misplaced behavior and tight coupling.

Find all instances: Search for methods that primarily read/manipulate another object's fields.

Fix correctly: Move the behavior onto the object that owns the data, or introduce a method there.

Constraints: Preserve behavior; keep encapsulation intact.

Acceptance: Behavior lives with its data. Ensure tests pass after the move.

checks.question: Does a single conceptual change require edits across many files or duplicated conditional sites (shotgun surgery)? (ARC-003)

onYes.title: Fix shotgun surgery (ARC-003): consolidate behind one abstraction
onYes.prompt:
Problem: When one change ripples across many files, the responsibility is scattered and error-prone.

Find all instances: Search for logic/decisions duplicated across many sites that must change together.

Fix correctly: Consolidate the responsibility behind a single abstraction or extension point so one change is localized.

Constraints: Preserve behavior. Don't over-abstract beyond the real variation (ARC-016).

Acceptance: The change is localized to one place. Add/keep tests covering the consolidated behavior.

checks.question: Do modules/packages import each other directly or indirectly (circular module dependency)? (ARC-004)

onYes.title: Fix circular dependency (ARC-004): break the cycle via inversion
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Cyclic dependencies couple modules tightly, hampering builds, testing, and reuse.

Find all instances: Search the module/package dependency graph for direct or indirect cycles.

Fix correctly: Break cycles using interfaces, dependency inversion, events, or by extracting a shared module both depend on.

Constraints: Preserve behavior; verify the build/dependency graph is acyclic after.

Acceptance: No dependency cycles remain. Add a build/architecture check if available; ensure tests pass.

checks.question: Do lower layers depend on higher layers, does UI reach into persistence, or does domain logic call infrastructure directly (layer violation)? (ARC-005)

onYes.title: Fix layer violation (ARC-005): route through intended boundaries
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Layering violations couple concerns that should be isolated, eroding maintainability and testability.

Find all instances: Search for lower layers referencing higher layers, UI accessing persistence directly, or domain code invoking infrastructure.

Fix correctly: Route access through the intended abstractions (e.g. domain depends on interfaces; infrastructure implements them).

Constraints: Preserve behavior; introduce interfaces/adapters as needed (ARC-007/ARC-020).

Acceptance: Dependencies respect layer boundaries. Add an architecture test/check where feasible; ensure tests pass.

checks.question: Are domain decisions, invariants, pricing, authorization, or workflows implemented in controllers/UI handlers (business logic in controller/UI handler)? (ARC-006)

onYes.title: Fix business logic in controllers (ARC-006): move to domain/application services
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Business logic in controllers/UI is hard to test/reuse and gets duplicated across entry points.

Find all instances: Search controllers/handlers for domain rules, invariants, pricing, authorization, or workflow logic.

Fix correctly: Move business behavior into application/domain services; keep controllers thin (parse, delegate, format).

Constraints: Preserve behavior. Centralize duplicated rules (ARC-013).

Acceptance: Controllers are thin; logic lives in services. Add/keep service-level tests for the moved logic.

checks.question: Do domain entities or rules directly perform SQL, HTTP, filesystem, or storage operations (persistence logic mixed into domain logic)? (ARC-007)

onYes.title: Fix persistence in domain (ARC-007): separate via repositories/adapters
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Mixing persistence/infrastructure into domain logic couples the domain to storage/IO, hurting testability.

Find all instances: Search domain entities/rules for direct SQL/HTTP/filesystem/storage calls.

Fix correctly: Move storage concerns behind repositories/gateways/adapters; keep the domain pure and dependency-inverted.

Constraints: Preserve behavior. Coordinate with layer boundaries (ARC-005).

Acceptance: Domain logic is storage-agnostic. Add unit tests for the domain without infrastructure.

checks.question: Are there global mutable variables, static registries, ambient config, or implicit context affecting behavior (hidden global state)? (ARC-008)

onYes.title: Fix hidden global state (ARC-008): inject dependencies, make state explicit
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Hidden global state creates implicit coupling, order-dependence, and concurrency bugs.

Find all instances: Search for global mutable variables, static registries/singletons, ambient config, and implicit context.

Fix correctly: Inject dependencies explicitly and make state explicit (scoped services, passed context).

Constraints: Preserve behavior. Combine with parallel-state isolation (CON-008) and service-locator fix (ARC-009).

Acceptance: State/dependencies are explicit. Add tests that no longer rely on global mutation.

checks.question: Are dependencies obtained via implicit global lookups (singletons/service locators) that hide dependencies and make tests order-dependent (singleton/service locator abuse)? (ARC-009)

onYes.title: Fix service-locator abuse (ARC-009): use explicit dependency injection
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Service-locator/singleton lookups hide real dependencies and cause fragile, order-dependent tests.

Find all instances: Search for static/global service lookups inside business logic.

Fix correctly: Inject dependencies explicitly via constructor/parameters instead of locating them globally.

Constraints: Preserve behavior. Coordinate with hidden-global-state (ARC-008).

Acceptance: Dependencies are injected, not located. Add tests that supply dependencies explicitly.

checks.question: Must APIs be called in a specific order but the order is not encoded or validated (undocumented temporal coupling)? (ARC-010)

onYes.title: Fix temporal coupling (ARC-010): encode required ordering
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Hidden call-order requirements cause misuse bugs that compile fine but fail at runtime.

Find all instances: Search for APIs requiring a specific call sequence (init-then-use, open-then-write) without enforcement.

Fix correctly: Encode ordering in types/state machines/builders or add explicit precondition checks that fail clearly when misused.

Constraints: Preserve behavior for correct sequences.

Acceptance: Misordered use is prevented or clearly rejected. Add a test calling APIs out of order asserting a clear failure.

checks.question: Are config keys, environment reads, constants, defaults, and parsing scattered across modules (configuration scattered across code)? (ARC-011)

onYes.title: Fix scattered configuration (ARC-011): centralize typed config with validation
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Scattered config reads cause drift, duplicate defaults, and inconsistent validation.

Find all instances: Search for repeated config-key reads, env reads, constants, and parsing across modules.

Fix correctly: Centralize configuration into typed, validated config objects loaded at startup; inject where needed.

Constraints: Config over hardcoding; values hot-reloadable where the project expects it. Validate at startup (OPS-009).

Acceptance: Config is centralized and validated. Add a test for config validation; ensure modules read from the central config.

checks.question: Are production/staging/dev values, regions, paths, credentials, hostnames, ports, or feature assumptions hard-coded (hard-coded environment assumption)? (ARC-012)

onYes.title: Fix hard-coded environment assumptions (ARC-012): externalize and validate
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Hard-coded environment values break across deployments and can leak credentials.

Find all instances: Search for hard-coded environment-specific values (URLs, regions, paths, hostnames, ports, env-specific flags) and credentials.

Fix correctly: Externalize environment-specific values to configuration and validate them at startup. Move secrets to managed storage (CSP-001).

Constraints: Config over hardcoding. Never commit secrets.

Acceptance: Environment values come from config and are validated. Add a startup validation test; confirm no hard-coded env values remain.

checks.question: Is the same pricing, eligibility, permission, validation, or state-transition rule implemented in multiple places (duplicate business rule)? (ARC-013)

onYes.title: Fix duplicate business rule (ARC-013): single authoritative implementation
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Duplicated business rules drift and produce inconsistent results.

Find all instances: Search for the same rule (pricing/eligibility/permission/validation/state-transition) implemented in more than one place.

Fix correctly: Create one authoritative implementation and call it everywhere; remove the duplicates.

Constraints: Preserve the correct rule semantics; reconcile any differences deliberately.

Acceptance: The rule has a single implementation. Add tests for the rule and confirm all call sites use it.

checks.question: Are modules changed for unrelated reasons (formatting, auth, storage, business logic, presentation), indicating mixed responsibilities causing divergent change (ARC-014)? (ARC-014)

onYes.title: Fix mixed responsibilities (ARC-014): split by reason to change
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Modules mixing unrelated responsibilities change for many reasons, increasing risk and merge conflicts.

Find all instances: Search for modules combining unrelated concerns (e.g. auth + storage + presentation).

Fix correctly: Split modules by responsibility and reason-to-change.

Constraints: Preserve behavior; refactor incrementally with tests. Avoid speculative splits (ARC-016).

Acceptance: Modules have single, cohesive responsibilities. Ensure tests pass after the split.

checks.question: Are there domain objects with only fields while invariants/behavior live in procedural services (anemic domain behavior)? (ARC-015)

onYes.title: Fix anemic domain (ARC-015): move invariant behavior into domain objects
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Anemic models scatter invariants in services, letting objects exist in invalid states.

Find all instances: Search for data-only domain objects whose invariants/behavior live in external procedural code.

Fix correctly: Move invariant-preserving behavior into the domain objects (or cohesive domain services) so invalid states are unrepresentable.

Constraints: Preserve behavior. Keep persistence concerns out of the domain (ARC-007).

Acceptance: Domain objects enforce their invariants. Add unit tests asserting invalid state is rejected by the object.

checks.question: Are there abstractions, extension points, generic frameworks, or options with only one real use case (speculative generality)? (ARC-016)

onYes.title: Fix speculative generality (ARC-016): remove unused abstraction
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Abstractions built for imagined future needs add complexity without value.

Find all instances: Search for generic interfaces/frameworks/options/extension points with a single concrete implementation/use.

Fix correctly: Remove the unused abstraction and inline the single case until real variation exists.

Constraints: Don't remove abstractions with genuine multiple uses or external contracts.

Acceptance: Unjustified abstractions are removed. Ensure tests pass and the code is simpler.

checks.question: Must callers know internal storage, protocol, vendor, cache, or implementation details to use a component (leaky abstraction)? (ARC-017)

onYes.title: Fix leaky abstraction (ARC-017): hide details behind a stable contract
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Leaky abstractions force callers to depend on internals, coupling them to implementation.

Find all instances: Search for components whose callers must know storage/protocol/vendor/cache details.

Fix correctly: Hide implementation details behind a stable contract/interface; expose intent, not mechanism.

Constraints: Preserve behavior. Coordinate with vendor isolation (ARC-020).

Acceptance: Callers depend only on the contract. Add tests against the interface; confirm internals aren't exposed.

checks.question: Are inheritance hierarchies used mainly for behavior reuse or optional feature combinations where composition fits better (inheritance where composition fits better)? (ARC-018)

onYes.title: Fix inheritance misuse (ARC-018): prefer composition/strategy
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Inheritance for reuse creates rigid hierarchies and fragile base classes.

Find all instances: Search for inheritance used for code reuse or to mix optional features rather than true is-a relationships.

Fix correctly: Prefer composition, strategy, or delegation for behavior variation.

Constraints: Preserve behavior. Keep genuine is-a relationships as inheritance.

Acceptance: Reuse uses composition where appropriate. Ensure tests pass after refactor.

checks.question: Do interfaces force clients to implement or depend on methods they do not use (fat interface)? (ARC-019)

onYes.title: Fix fat interface (ARC-019): split by client need
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Fat interfaces couple clients to methods they don't need (violating interface segregation).

Find all instances: Search for large interfaces whose implementers/clients use only a subset.

Fix correctly: Split interfaces by client need/responsibility into smaller cohesive contracts.

Constraints: Preserve behavior. Maintain backward compatibility for public interfaces (API-001).

Acceptance: Interfaces are cohesive and client-focused. Ensure tests pass after the split.

checks.question: Does core domain logic depend directly on vendor SDKs, cloud APIs, framework types, or platform services (vendor/platform lock-in in core logic)? (ARC-020)

onYes.title: Fix vendor lock-in in core (ARC-020): isolate behind adapters
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Core logic coupled to vendor/platform specifics is hard to test and migrate.

Find all instances: Search core/domain code for direct dependencies on vendor SDKs/cloud APIs/framework types/platform services.

Fix correctly: Isolate vendor/platform details behind adapter interfaces owned by the core; depend on those interfaces.

Constraints: Preserve behavior. Coordinate with layer boundaries (ARC-005).

Acceptance: Core logic is vendor-agnostic behind adapters. Add unit tests for the core using fakes instead of the vendor SDK.
